chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Opinion: jazz was not only from New Orleans
summary: Holmes argues that jazz was played by Black people everywhere, recalling his mother humming spirituals.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Sure, it was. Sure. That's what killed me about this thing, talking about Jazz from New Orleans. It might be from there, but they were not the first ones to play it. Jazz has always been played amongst Black people. It's always been. Because I could... Man, when I was a little boy and my Mama would be ironing clothes or something, you know, and I'd be crawling around the floor, and she'd be ironing her clothes and just humming one of
them spirituals or something. You talk about your Jazz! You would have to tap your foot. And she was just hummin' a spiritual. But I mean, the Jazz was there.

So I mean, you can't... I don't see how they can pinpoint it to one particular area in the country, when the same thing was happening all over the country! Any place you go where there were Black people, they were singing and doing the same thing. And it was not a whole lot of communication in them days like there is today. But that stuff got around. Yeah, it got around all right. I don't know...
